product.summary: A phone app that tracks kitchen food from scanned grocery receipts and suggests meals that use it before it spoils.

source.quote: A phone app that keeps track of what is in your kitchen and suggests meals that use up food before it spoils.

evidence.value: Still an idea; nothing built yet

source.quote: Pantry Pal is still an idea. Nothing is built yet.

evidence.value: Landing page and a waitlist of 340 email sign-ups

source.quote: We have a landing page and a waitlist with 340 email sign-ups
Nothing is built yet.
Our hope is 2,000 people in the beta

projected.what: users by the end of next year (founders' guess)

source.quote: 10,000 users by the end of next year, but these are guesses
Users sign in with email.
We store the food they buy and the meals they cook.

source.why: Purchase and meal history is personal data whose leak can embarrass people; allergy data, if stored later, would be health data and make it high.

retention.value: receipt photos deleted once the items are read (promised publicly)

source.quote: Receipt photos should be deleted once the items are read; we promised this on the landing page.
We are two founders, Maya Okafor and Luis Brandt
Maya is a product designer

skills.value: backend development; has built two small Django apps (Luis)

source.quote: Luis is a backend developer who has built two small Django apps.

skills.value: no experience running production systems with real users

source.quote: Neither of us has run anything in production with real users at night.

operating_capacity.value: part-time, about 15 hours a week each, next to day jobs

source.quote: We both work on this part-time, about 15 hours a week each, next to our day jobs.

build.value: $12,000 in total for the first year, from savings, everything included

source.quote: We are paying for everything from our savings: $12,000 in total for the first year, everything included.
We would like hosting to stay under $150 a month until we know people want this.

constraints.text: Total spend in the first year stays within the founders' $12,000 savings

source.quote: $12,000 in total for the first year, everything included

constraints.text: Delete receipt photos once their items are read, as promised on the landing page

source.quote: Receipt photos should be deleted once the items are read; we promised this on the landing page.

goals.note: Get a beta out fast to learn whether people use it

source.quote: Above all, we need to learn quickly whether people use it, so getting a beta out fast is the first thing.
Keeping costs low comes right after that.

goals.note: Simple to operate; no nights fixing servers

source.quote: We do not want to spend nights fixing servers, so anything we run should be simple to operate.

goals.note: Easy to change often after the beta

source.quote: We will need to change things often after the beta, so the design should be easy to change.

unknowns.question: Will Pantry Pal store users' food allergies?
unknowns.why_it_matters: Allergy data is health data: it raises sensitivity to high and brings stricter rules on consent, storage and security.

unknowns.question: Which country will the beta launch in first?
unknowns.why_it_matters: Germany brings GDPR and Canada PIPEDA; the answer decides the hosting region and the privacy duties.

unknowns.question: How many receipts does a typical user scan per week?
unknowns.why_it_matters: Reading receipts is the main processing load and cost; it sizes the receipt-reading service.

unknowns.question: Which outside services, if any, will the product use?
unknowns.why_it_matters: None is named; any receipt reader or mail service is a later design choice.

unknowns.question: What load is there now?
unknowns.why_it_matters: Nothing is in users' hands yet, so there is none to measure.

unknowns.question: When are the busiest moments?
unknowns.why_it_matters: No peak is named; at beta size a peak would not change the design.

unknowns.question: How fast must the app answer?
unknowns.why_it_matters: No speed target is named; suggestions come once an evening.

unknowns.question: What availability does the beta need?
unknowns.why_it_matters: With no one on call at night, the answer would only tune how much managed hosting to pay for.

unknowns.question: How much data may the beta lose?
unknowns.why_it_matters: Nothing is stored yet; ordinary backups cover any plausible answer.

unknowns.question: How fast must the beta come back after a failure?
unknowns.why_it_matters: No one is on call; any plausible answer leads to the same simple setup.

unknowns.question: Does anyone else receive users' data?
unknowns.why_it_matters: No one is named; processors are a later design choice.

unknowns.question: Are security controls needed beyond email sign-in?
unknowns.why_it_matters: None is asked for; the allergy question is where this would change.

unknowns.question: Are there named threats?
unknowns.why_it_matters: Nothing is built and none is named.

unknowns.question: Does any certification or audit apply?
unknowns.why_it_matters: None is asked for; the legal doubt is about allergies and the launch country.

assumptions.text: The beta is one region and one small database.
assumptions.why: Two part-time founders, a few thousand projected users and no stated peaks.
